picks.thesis: Markets are in a pre-Nvidia/pre-FOMC holding pattern with a risk-on tilt driven by tech momentum; we hold our existing AMD position and add a behavioral bet on the crypto-brokerage theme via HOOD, which is showing clear momentum and a structural catalyst, while keeping significant cash to respect the drawdown ladder.
picks.justification: The macro snapshot shows a steep yield curve, normal VIX, and a broad rally led by tech and crypto-exposed names (HOOD +15.8%, MSTR +14.5%, COIN +9.5%). This is a 'risk-on' rotation within the market, not a broad beta move. Our existing long call position in AMD is a bet on the AI/Data Center theme, which remains intact. We are adding a position in HOOD because the behavioral edge is clear: retail and institutional flows into crypto are surging, and HOOD is the primary listed beneficiary. The structural catalyst is the new Goldman Sachs target and the technical breakout. We are wrong if this flow reverses sharply, which we will monitor via COIN and BTC price action. We are leaving 50% in cash because we are in a drawdown and must respect the risk budget.

positions.thesis: We hold our existing long call position. The thesis is an analytical edge: AMD's MI300X data-center ramp is underappreciated relative to NVDA's supply constraints, and the recent analyst upgrade confirms this variant perception. The three-sentence test: We are long AMD because the market is underestimating its AI server market share gains. It is mispriced because of a behavioral anchoring bias to NVDA as the only AI winner, which persists because sell-side analysts are slow to revise their models for a duopoly. We are wrong if AMD fails to guide for >$4B in Data Center GPU revenue on its next earnings call or if the stock closes below $400 by 2026-10-03.
positions.invalidation: AMD closes below $400 (a breach of the recent breakout level and the thesis's fundamental support) OR the next company update shows Data Center GPU revenue guidance below $4B, by 2026-10-03.
